content: 1. Jafa K, McElroy P, et al. (2009) published a study in PLoS One (Volume 4, Issue 5, Article e5416). 2. Motshabi LC, Pengpid S, et al. (2011) investigated the utilization of HIV counseling and testing, as well as the attitudes of male inmates in a South African prison, in the Journal of Social Aspects of HIV/AIDS (Volume 8, Issue 3, Pages 107-114). 3. De Voux A, Spaulding AC, et al. (2012) provided empirical evidence supporting early identification of HIV through jail-based testing in PLoS One (Volume 7, Issue 5, Article e37603). 4. The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC), UNAIDS, and WHO (2009) released a technical paper on HIV testing and counseling in prisons and other closed settings. 5. Beckwith CG, Liu T, et al. (2010) examined HIV risk behaviors before and after counseling and testing in jail in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes (Volume 53, Issue 4, Pages 485-490). 6. MacGowan R, Margolis A, et al. (2009) studied voluntary rapid HIV testing in jails, publishing their findings in Sexually Transmitted Diseases (Volume 36, Supplement 2, Pages S9-S13). 7. Beckwith CG, Bazerman L, et al. (2011) evaluated a routine opt-out rapid HIV testing program in Rhode Island, with results published in AIDS Education and Prevention (Volume 23, Issue 3, Pages 96-109). 8. Tartaro C, Levy MP (2012) assessed an HIV testing program in a jail setting, presenting results and recommendations in The Prison Journal (Volume 93, Issue 1, Pages 57-79). 9. Andrinopoulos K, Kerrigan D, et al. (2010) established an HIV/sexually transmitted disease program and reported infection prevalence among incarcerated men in Jamaica in the International Journal of STD and AIDS (Volume 21, Issue 2, Pages 114-119). 10. Arp W (2009) explored the intersection of race, incarceration, and HIV/AIDS in Louisiana, emphasizing risky sexual behaviors and the need for mandatory testing, in Race, Class, and Gender (Volume 16, Issues 1-2, Pages 228-237). 11. Kavasery R, Maru DS, et al. (2009) conducted a prospective controlled trial on routine opt-out HIV testing in a men’s jail, with findings published in PLoS One (Volume 4, Issue 11, Article e8056). 12. Strick LB, MacGowan J, et al. (2011) reported on HIV screening of male inmates during prison intake medical evaluations in Washington (2006-2010) in the Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (Volume 60, Issue 24, Pages 811-813). 13. Javanbakht M, Murphy R, et al. (2007) examined the prevalence of sexually transmitted infections and HIV among incarcerated men who have sex with men (2000-2005) in Sexually Transmitted Infections (Volume 36, Supplement 2, Pages S17-S21). 14. Tuli K, Kerndt PR (2009) analyzed the cost-effectiveness of preventing sexually transmitted infections among incarcerated men who have sex with men in Sexually Transmitted Diseases (Volume 36, Supplement 2, Pages S41-S48). 15. Roberson DW, White BL (2009) identified factors influencing adherence to antiretroviral therapy among HIV-infected female inmates in the Journal of the Association of Nurses in AIDS Care (Volume 20, Issue 1, Pages 50-61). 16. Small W, Wood E, et al. (2009) conducted a qualitative study on the impact of incarceration on adherence to HIV treatment among HIV-positive injection drug users, published in AIDS Care (Volume 21, Issue 6, Pages 708-714). 17. Shalihu N, Pretorius L, et al. (2014) described barriers to antiretroviral therapy adherence among Namibian prisoners in AIDS Care (published ahead of print). 18. Catz SL, Thibodeau L, et al. (2011) explored the prevention needs of HIV-positive men and women awaiting release from prison in AIDS Behavior (Volume 16, Issue 1, Pages 108-120). 19. Fontana L, Beckerman A (2007) highlighted the primary care treatment needs and experiences of recently released individuals with HIV/AIDS in the Journal of Health Care for the Poor and Underserved (Volume 18, Issue 3, Pages 699-714). 20. Wohl DA, Scheyett A, et al. (2011) compared intensive case management with comprehensive pre-release discharge planning for linking HIV-infected prisoners to care, publishing their randomized trial results in AIDS Behavior (Volume 15, Issue 2, Pages 356-364). 21. Nunn A, Cornwall A, et al. (2010) assessed the COMPASS program, which links HIV-positive jail inmates to treatment, care, and social services after release, in Journal of Urban Health (Volume 87, Issue 6, Pages 954-968). 22. Zaller ND, Holmes L, et al. (2008) evaluated linkage to treatment and supportive services among HIV-positive ex-offenders in Project Bridge, with findings published in the Journal of Health Care for the Poor and Underserved (Volume 19, Issue 2, Pages 522-531). 23. Seal DW, Margolis AD, et al. (2008) studied substance use and sexual behavior during incarceration among men aged 18-29, reporting prevalence and correlates in AIDS Behavior (Volume 12, Issue 1, Pages 27-40). 24. Milloy MJ, Kerr T, et al. (2013) found that incarceration is associated with syringe lending among active injection drug users with detectable plasma HIV-1 RNA, as reported in BMC Infectious Diseases (Volume 13, Article 565). 25. Moller LF, Van Den Bergh BJ, et al. (2008) examined the effects of health promotion on drug use among prisoners in Kyrgyzstan in the International Journal of Prisoner Health (Volume 4, Issue 3, Pages 124-133). 26. Roshanfekr P, Farnia M, et al. (2013) evaluated the effectiveness of harm reduction programs in seven Iranian prisons in the Iranian Journal of Public Health (Volume 42, Issue 12, Pages 1430-1437). 27. Ferrer-Castro V, Crespo-Leiro MR, et al. (2012) reviewed a ten-year experience with a needle exchange program at Pereiro de Aguiar Prison in Spain, publishing their findings in Revista Española de Sanidad Penitenciaria (Volume 14, Issue 1, Pages 3-11).
